When move dates don’t line up, you need a clear plan for your belongings as well as the move itself. Removals with storage can bridge that gap. Here are five named options to consider, starting with South West London Removals and its fixed quotation process.

  • South West London Removals: local moves with storage and packing
  • Matrix Moving Group: containerised storage with UK coverage
  • Warpspeed Removals & Storage: flexible storage between homes
  • Wimbledon Removals: local, national and office moves
  • Bournes: check current removals and storage services

1. South West London Removals: local moves with storage and packing

South West London Removals handles home and office moves across South West London and Surrey. We also arrange packing, short and long-term storage, and nationwide moves from the area.

Our team can quote after a recorded WhatsApp video survey. You show us the rooms, furniture and access, including stairs or a tight parking spot. We use those details to prepare a fixed quotation before moving day.

If your move needs a storage period, our short and long-term storage service can support a chain move, renovation or downsize. Collection and delivery are included on the business website.

Local access can change how a move is planned. A flat near West Brompton may need different loading arrangements from a house in Surrey. We ask about the property and access during the survey, so the quote can reflect the work involved.

For moves further into Surrey, see our Epsom Removals service. If your route is near Kingston, our Norbiton Removals page covers that local area.

Furniture is wrapped in blankets and shrink wrap before it leaves the room. The crew arrives with protection materials and a loading plan. Packing is available too, including help with belongings that need extra care.

The business website includes a customer comment praising clear updates and a price that stayed as quoted. That reflects the points worth settling before any booking: what the price covers, how storage is arranged and who will update you if dates change.

2. Matrix Moving Group: containerised storage with UK coverage

Matrix Moving Group describes its storage as secure containerised storage, with facilities spread across the UK. Its storage information also describes sealed units in temperature-controlled warehouse space, for short or long stays.

That combination may suit a household that needs storage beyond the local move itself. The company says it can arrange delivery to destinations across the UK or worldwide, and it describes removals support across London and the Home Counties.

Before agreeing a plan, ask how the storage unit is assigned and how your goods will be recorded. Check what notice is needed if you want to access belongings, and how collection or redelivery will work when your new address is ready.

Matrix describes a 24-hour notice period for access to stored effects. It also says staff can help add or remove items, or arrange delivery of some or all of the stored belongings. Confirm the current terms for your booking before relying on a specific access arrangement.

For a move that needs packing, the company describes professionally trained removal teams using packing techniques. That may help if you want the same provider to handle the move and prepare furniture for storage, rather than arranging separate crews.

Storage conditions matter most for items that will stay put for a while. Ask how furniture is wrapped, whether the unit stays sealed and what cover applies while goods are in storage. Get the answers in writing alongside the removal quotation.

3. Warpspeed Removals & Storage: flexible storage between homes

Warpspeed Removals & Storage describes its storage as flexible, with collection and delivery. The service is framed for people who need a little room between homes, such as when sale and purchase dates do not match.

The company’s site describes moves across Surrey, Sussex and Kent, with wider coverage across Great Britain. It also names Reigate, Redhill, Dorking and Horley among the towns it serves.

Its enquiry process starts with an inventory form. You can add videos to show belongings and access, then the team reviews the details before preparing an estimate. An enquiry does not reserve a booking; the move is confirmed after you accept the estimate and agree the arrangements.

That sequence is useful when your date is still taking shape. You can ask about the move before completion is confirmed, then settle the booking once the dates and storage period are clearer.

Warpspeed describes packing support for a whole home, fragile items or customer-packed belongings. It also shares customer comments about careful packing and clear pricing. Treat reviews as one part of your decision, then check the written scope for your own move.

When you compare a flexible storage plan, ask how long the initial period runs and how delivery is booked. Also check what happens if the handover date shifts. Those points can affect the cost and timing of a move, even when the storage itself sounds straightforward.

4. Wimbledon Removals: local, national and office moves

Wimbledon Removals describes local and national moves for houses, flats and offices. Its service information also says it operates seven days a week.

That range may make it worth considering for a move with a less usual schedule, such as an office relocation outside a standard weekday. For a home move, the property type matters too: a top-floor flat and a house with direct access can need different plans.

If storage is part of your move, ask for the storage period and the handling plan to be set out in the quotation. Confirm who collects your belongings, how delivery is arranged and what happens if your new address is not ready on the planned date.

For any provider, get a clear inventory or written description of what is moving. Include large furniture and fragile items. If dismantling or reassembly is needed, agree who will do it before booking rather than assuming it is part of a standard move.

Our West Brompton Removals page gives local information for moves where flat access and loading need attention. Those details are worth discussing early, whether you are moving across the area or into storage.

5. Bournes: check current removals and storage services

Bournes is another named company to assess when you compare a move that may need storage. Confirm the current service scope for your route and dates before you treat it as a combined removals and storage booking.

Ask for a written outline of the move, the storage term and the return delivery plan. If your move depends on a property chain or renovation, make sure the plan explains how a date change is handled.

Insurance needs careful checking too. Ask what cover applies during loading, transport and storage, and what you need to declare about high-value or fragile goods. A company’s general insurance wording may not answer every question about your own belongings.

We plan access and furniture handling as part of the quotation process. If your move is in Claygate, our Claygate Removals page gives local service details to help you describe the property and route.

A clear quote should set out what the crew will move and what happens if the dates change. Read the terms alongside the price, then ask for any agreed storage or delivery details to be confirmed in writing.

Frequently asked questions

Can I use removals with storage if my completion dates change?

Yes, storage can bridge a gap when your move-out and move-in dates do not match. Tell the provider what dates are confirmed and which may change. Ask how the storage period is extended, how delivery is rebooked and whether the quotation covers those changes. Get the agreed plan in writing before the collection date.

What should I ask about storage before booking?

Ask how your belongings will be packed and stored, what access arrangements apply and how delivery is booked. Check the expected storage term and what happens if it needs to run longer. Ask what insurance applies while goods are in storage, and confirm how fragile or high-value items should be recorded.

Can one company handle packing, moving and storage?

Some providers describe support that combines moving with packing or storage, but the scope differs. Ask whether packing covers the full home, selected rooms or fragile items only. Confirm who collects the packed goods and whether delivery to your new home is part of the agreed plan.

How do I compare removal quotations fairly?

Give each provider the same information about your inventory, access, addresses and storage dates. Compare the written scope as well as the price: check packing, storage, redelivery and insurance terms. A quote based on a video survey can help the team see stairs, furniture and access before setting a fixed price.

Choose a plan that covers the whole move

For a South West London or Surrey move that needs storage, start with South West London Removals if you want a fixed quotation based on a recorded video survey. Send your route, likely dates and storage needs through the website so we can review the scope with you.
